text:
maya: Hey team — incoming customer request from Kestrel. They want a 12B model (Raptor-12B) onboarded into Dedicated with 8-bit quant and a strict p95 latency goal of 180ms for short chat flows. Can we triage?

jia: Pinged product for context. Do we have a reference checkpoint or is this a new export? :eyes:

maya: They provided a HF tarball and a TF->PT conversion script. Link: https://kestrel.example/raptor-12b.tar.gz

simon: Quick questions: training tokenizer standard? vocab size? any legacy custom ops?

maya: Tokenizer is SentencePiece, vocab 50240. No custom ops reported, but conversion script touches Attention mask handling.

eli: OK. My rough plan: 1) run basic sanity (load, sample), 2) run FP16 perf baseline on A10, 3) 8-bit quantize experiment (GPTQ-ish), 4) run our eval suite (safety, instruction-following, llm-eval), 5) quality regressions vs Redwood baseline.

carla: Priority? Customer says P1 for Dedicated in 3 weeks. We should confirm SLOs and whether Dedicated GPU type is A100 or A10.

maya: Customer will be on Dedicated A10 pools initially. P1 timeline confirmed.

jia: I'll take step 1 + tokenizer validation. Can you drop conversion logs here when you run it? Also add a small unit test: `print(model.generate('Hello')[:80])` to catch obvious decode issues.

eli: Starting FP16 load on a dev A10 node now. ETA ~30m. If FP16 looks fine, I'll snapshot baseline perf.

-- 25m later --

deploy-bot: build:raptor-load-1 succeeded (job: load-and-smoke-test)

eli: FP16 load succeeded. Sample output looks coherent. Baseline p50/p95 (1-token step) on A10: 22ms / 120ms for chat length=64 with batching=1. Memory headroom ~13GB free.

jia: Tokenization tests passed. Conversion note: the conversion script rewrites attention mask dim order, added a small fix. Pushed patch to repo.

carla: Good. Next: quant strategy. We need to pick method (GPTQ, AWQ, or static 8-bit quant). Customer prefers 8-bit for cost but wants minimal quality loss.

simon: Suggest we try AWQ first (faster, good quality) then fallback to GPTQ if regressions show up. Also run 4-bit nf4 as a stretch.

eli: I'll run AWQ 8-bit sweep with these params: `--bits 8 --group-size 128 --chunk-size 4096 --calib-samples 2048`. Will log eval metrics.

maya: Also add targeted evals: instruction-following (our 2k prompt set), factual accuracy (FEVER subset), and hallucination probes used in prior bringups. Customer cares about safety too.

-- later that day --

simon: AWQ 8-bit initial run done. Micro-benchmarks: p50/p95: 18ms / 140ms (chat len=64, b=1). So p95 worse than FP16 baseline. Need to check KV-cache decode path and batched path.

eli: Eval diff vs FP16 baseline: instruction-following drop ~1.8% absolute (from 86.4 -> 84.6), FEVER F1 drop 2.1. Safety gating: no new toxic outputs found in quick pass.

carla: For a P1 customer, a ~2% drop may be acceptable but depends on which prompts fail. We should run per-prompt regression to surface worst cases.

jia: Pushed a regression harness run. Attaching top 5 failure examples.

maya: Shared failures with Kestrel (sensitive prompts). They asked if we can try GPTQ to narrow regressions.

simon: OK. Queue GPTQ run but note it's slower to produce. Also disable group quant for some layers (attn + ln) to mitigate.

eli: Kicked off GPTQ with selective per-layer config. ETA ~2h. Will capture eval and perf.

-- next morning --

eli: GPTQ run complete. Quality: instruction-following back to 86.2 (near baseline). FEVER F1 +1. Best-case. Perf p50/p95: 24ms / 160ms (decode slower than AWQ). Memory use higher but still fits Dedicated A10 plan.

carla: Tradeoff summary: AWQ = best perf, small quality drop; GPTQ = near baseline quality, worse p95. Customer priority is cost+latency. We should propose two options to Kestrel.

maya: Drafting options: Option A (default): AWQ 8-bit + micro-regression guardrails + early-warning evals. Option B (conservative): GPTQ quant with tuned per-layer exclusions and slower p95 but higher quality. Ask customer which route and whether they'd accept canary release.

jia: Also recommended: enable prefix KV caching on route and batched decode tuning (we saw p95 jump under short chat). That will likely reduce p95 by ~20-30ms in practice. Add that to prescriptive plan.

simon: Operational checklist before Dedicated rollout:
- owner assigned (eli)
- conversion + tokenizer validated (done)
- quant method + artifacts stored in model-repo (artifact id: raptor-12b-awq-v1, raptor-12b-gptq-v1)
- regression report uploaded to S3 (link pasted)
- perf benchmark report and recommended autoscale config
- canary policy: 5% traffic for 48h then 25% then 100%
- alerting: quality regression (delta > 2% on instruction set), latency SLO breach, error spikes

maya: I'll coordinate with account team for canary approval and legal for any compliance checks.

carla: Kickoffs scheduled: canary next Tues at 17:00 UTC. Eli will own the deployment; Simon will monitor eval regressions.

eli: taking ownership. I'll upload quant artifacts and a small runbook to the model repo tonight.

deploy-bot: artifact-upload:raptor-12b-awq-v1 success

maya: Thanks all. Leaving notes here for follow-up: add 4-bit nf4 exploratory ticket, perf tuning for p95 via batching, and a post-canary eval run.

simon: LGTM. :thumbsup:

carla: Marking this thread as triaged. Will link to intake ticket: INT-4472 in the doc.

maya: closing the loop with Kestrel now.

-- end --
